- Concise Psychological Formulation:
  - Predisposing: History of eczema; prior dermatitis/eczema episodes.

  - Perpetuating: Scratching and skin-cracking perpetuating itch-scratch cycle; sleep disruption exacerbating daytime impairment.

Mental Health Care Plan Details
Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Obtain rapid relief from pruritus; improve sleep; resume normal functioning at work and activities (e.g., hiking).
- Clinical Goal(s): Control dermatitis symptoms within 7–10 days; improve sleep quality; reduce daytime concentration impairment; reassess response at follow-up.
- Actions (Patient): Use prescribed topical corticosteroid as directed; apply emollients regularly (bath/shower routine); consider and use antihistamines as advised; maintain a diary of potential triggers; avoid scratching; return for follow-up if not improved.
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe stronger topical corticosteroid; provide emollients and skin-care guidance; initiate antihistamine therapy (Fexofenadine today); discuss trigger-diary approach; advise on sun/skin care and avoidance of irritants; arrange follow-up appointment in 7–10 days; provide education on eczema management and CU (contact dermatitis) considerations; consider dermatology referral if insufficient improvement.

Secondary Problem:
- Sleep Disturbance related to pruritus:
  - Patient Goal(s): Better sleep and daytime functioning.
  - Clinical Goal(s): Sleep quality improved by resolution of nocturnal itch within 7–10 days.
  - Actions (Patient): Implement sleep-friendly skin-care routine; adhere to treatment plan; utilize non-pharmacologic sleep hygiene strategies as appropriate.
  - Actions (Clinician/GP): Reinforce sleep hygiene; monitor sleep-related symptoms at follow-up; adjust treatment plan if sleep does not improve.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: dermatitis/eczema management; use of emollients; proper topical steroid use; role of antihistamines in itch control; importance of trigger diary; recognition of potential contact/irritant dermatitis.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Worsening itch or rash despite treatment; spreading involvement; development of fever, painful cracking, oozing or pus; systemic symptoms.
- Coping Strategies: Regular emollient use; keep skin moisturized; avoid scratching; trigger diary to identify irritants/allergens; maintain routine for skin care; sleep hygiene practices.
